entities.name: Henry III, Count of Schauenburg-Holstein
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Henry III, Count of Schauenburg-Holstein, a pivotal figure in the complex dynastic and ecclesiastical politics of late medieval Northern Europe, served as Bishop of Osnabrück as Henry I from 1402 to 1410 and concurrently as Count of Holstein-Rendsburg from 1404 until his death on February 1, 1421. Born into the powerful House of Schauenburg, which held significant sway over the Duchy of Holstein, his career exemplifies the dual secular and spiritual authority common among prince-bishops in the Holy Roman Empire. His actions profoundly influenced the ongoing struggle for control over Schleswig, a critical border region between Denmark and the German states, shaping the political geography of the region for decades.

His tenure was marked by intense territorial disputes and diplomatic maneuvering, particularly concerning Schleswig. As Count of Holstein-Rendsburg, he inherited a long-standing conflict with the Danish crown. A major turning point occurred in 1409 when, following military pressures and intricate negotiations, Henry III was compelled to sign the Treaty of Kolding, ceding his rights to Schleswig to Queen Margaret I of Denmark. This treaty represented a significant, albeit temporary, Danish victory in the protracted Schleswig Question. Furthermore, his ecclesiastical role as Bishop of Osnabrück involved him in regional church administration and temporal governance of the prince-bishopric, balancing spiritual duties with the demands of a sovereign ruler.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Henry III played a crucial role in the regional power dynamics of Northern Europe, particularly through his involvement in the Schleswig Question, which led to the Treaty of Kolding and influenced subsequent Dano-German relations for centuries. His dual role as count and bishop also highlights the complex interplay of secular and ecclesiastical authority in the Holy Roman Empire.
